headline: GOLD $4,155 SILVER $62+ AS 9-9 FOMC SPLIT CONFIRMED IN MINUTES — SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE AT 50% PROBABILITY, METALS EXTEND RALLY
snippet: Gold held near $4,155 per ounce and silver traded above $62 on July 8 as the FOMC minutes from the June meeting confirmed a 9-9 split between members — with five members favouring a hike at the next meeting and the remaining four openly neutral, pushing the September rate hike probability to approximately 50% and providing a near-term floor for precious metals. The dollar weakened in response to the minutes, with XTB's metals desk noting that a genuinely divided Fed is historically more bullish for gold than a clean-dove outcome: uncertainty about the policy path sustains haven demand while delaying the USD strength that typically weighs on metals at cycle peaks. Junior mining equities are particularly sensitive to this dynamic — a prolonged pause with elevated inflation expectations compresses real rates without triggering the risk-off move that historically accompanies a tightening cycle.

headline: TOREX GOLD LOS REYES PEA: AFTER-TAX NPV $1.5B AND 37% IRR AT BASE CASE — $1.816B NPV AT SPOT, PFS STARTING H2 2026 (TSX:TXG)
snippet: Torex Gold Resources (TSX:TXG) released July 7 a Preliminary Economic Assessment on the Los Reyes deposit — part of the broader Media Luna complex in Guerrero, Mexico — that returned an after-tax NPV5% of US$1.5 billion and a 37% IRR at base-case metal prices, climbing to an after-tax NPV of US$1.816 billion and 42.7% IRR at prices 10% above base case (materially below current spot). A Pre-Feasibility Study is scheduled to commence in H2 2026, setting up Los Reyes as a second discrete production decision following Media Luna's successful ramp-up to commercial production in 2024. The PEA numbers frame Los Reyes as a high-margin, high-return extension of an already-de-risked operating complex — reducing the capital uncertainty discount that typically weighs on development-stage mining PEAs.

headline: TUDOR GOLD DISCOVERS SILVER BRECCIA SYSTEM AT TREATY CREEK — CBS-26-08 PIERCES UNTESTED HIGH-FLUID-FLOW CORRIDOR IN BC'S GOLDEN TRIANGLE (TSXV:TUD)
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSXV:TUD) announced July 7 that drill hole CBS-26-08 at the Treaty Creek Project in BC's Golden Triangle has pierced a new high-grade silver breccia system within a structural corridor identified by the 2026 program as a high-fluid-flow conduit — a geological architecture consistent with bonanza-grade precious metals concentrations in BC porphyry systems. The silver breccia discovery is spatially distinct from the Treaty Creek copper-gold porphyry resource and represents a potentially separate mineralization style within the same camp, raising the possibility of multiple deposit types on a single large-scale tenure. Treaty Creek is one of the largest undeveloped gold-copper porphyry systems in the Golden Triangle and the silver breccia result opens a new exploration vector ahead of any economic study.

headline: GLOBEX BALD HILL DRILLS 16.65% SB OVER 5.05M INCL. 33.40% OVER 1.10M — LAC ESCALE 52.2MT LITHIUM ROYALTY DRILLING STARTS (TSX:GMX)
snippet: Globex Mining Enterprises (TSX:GMX) reported July 6 drill hole BH-26-25 at Bald Hill in Quebec returned 16.65% Sb over 5.05 metres including 33.40% Sb over 1.10 metres — grades that rank among the highest-grade antimony intercepts reported in Canada, where the metal's strategic classification under US and EU critical minerals policy is driving renewed exploration interest. On the same date, Globex confirmed that drilling has commenced at the Lac Escale Lithium Royalty in Quebec — a 52.2 million tonne deposit at 1.08% Li2O where Globex holds a royalty interest. The dual announcement — critical antimony at Bald Hill plus battery-metals royalty activation at Lac Escale — positions Globex across two of the most policy-relevant mineral categories of 2026 in a single news cycle.

headline: ALKANE DELIVERS 168,337 OZ AUEQ IN FY2026 — TOP HALF OF 160K–175K GUIDANCE, GOLD-ANTIMONY DUAL REVENUE IN JUNE QUARTER (ASX:ALK)
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX:ALK) reported July 8 that its Tomingley Gold Operations in New South Wales delivered 168,337 gold-equivalent ounces in FY2026 — landing in the top half of the 160,000–175,000 oz AuEq guidance range — with the June quarter contributing 42,491 oz AuEq as the integrated gold-antimony production model continued to generate dual-commodity revenue at a time when antimony commands a strategic premium. The FY2026 result demonstrates that a producing Australian gold miner is now generating antimony as a meaningful revenue contributor alongside gold — a business model that was previously non-existent at small-to-mid cap scale — and that the critical minerals angle is additive rather than speculative when attached to an already-profitable gold operation.

headline: LITHIUM DROPS TO 3-MONTH LOW AS CATL JIANXIAWO RESTART LOOMS — CNY 151,750/T CARBONATE, 46,000T LCE/YR CAPACITY IN PLAY
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate prices slid to a three-month low near CNY 151,750 per tonne in early July 2026 after market speculation emerged that CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine — a 46,000 tonne LCE per year operation representing approximately 3% of global supply — could restart following a land pre-approval issued June 2026 and valid through June 2029. The potential restart adds a significant supply overhang at precisely the moment when EV demand growth has decelerated sharply (global EV sales up just 0.9% year-on-year in January–May 2026), compounding the demand-side headwind Andy Home identified last week. For battery-metals investors, the CATL restart risk represents a structural supply threat rather than a cyclical one: pre-approved mine capacity that can be activated on short notice is a different order of uncertainty than project-stage mine supply, and the 3-year permit window means the overhang persists through 2029.

headline: 89% OF CENTRAL BANKS PLAN HIGHER GOLD RESERVES — PBOC AT 2,300+ TONNES AFTER 18 STRAIGHT MONTHS BUYING, DOLLAR SHARE FALLING
snippet: An FXStreet de-dollarization analysis published July 7 highlights that 89% of central banks surveyed by the World Gold Council expect global gold reserves to rise over the next 12 months, 45% report their own holdings are increasing, and 74% anticipate a further decline in the US dollar's share of global reserves — a trifecta that has historically preceded multi-year structural gold bull markets. China's People's Bank of China is now the emblematic case study: 18 consecutive months of reported purchases has taken official holdings above 2,300 tonnes, and the PBOC's stated intent to continue diversification away from USD-denominated assets means the single largest marginal buyer in the gold market is both price-insensitive and structurally committed. For junior mining investors, the critical implication is that the current gold price environment is underpinned by sovereign-level structural demand — not just speculative positioning — which reduces the probability of the sharp reversals that historically wiped out leveraged junior positions in previous bull cycles.

headline: GOLD SWOT: PALLADIUM SURGES ON SOUTH AFRICA SUPPLY FEARS — GDX 30%+ BELOW METAL-IMPLIED VALUE AFTER 57K PAYROLL MISS
snippet: Kitco's weekly Gold SWOT analysis for the week of July 6 notes that precious metals across the board — gold, silver, palladium, and platinum — responded positively to June non-farm payrolls of just 57,000 versus the 110,000 consensus forecast, a miss that materially reduced Fed tightening expectations and drove the dollar lower in the same session. Palladium's surge is separately identified as being driven by South African supply disruption fears — PGM production in the Bushveld Complex has been running below nameplate capacity due to ongoing power and cost pressures — while the most striking statistic in the SWOT framework is that the GDX gold miners ETF remains more than 30% below its metal-implied value on conventional NAV multiples, suggesting that even after a strong run in senior miners, the equity leverage to the gold price has not been fully priced in by institutional investors.

headline: DIESEL AT $70/BBL ADDS 15-20% TO OPEN-PIT CASH COSTS — AFRICA AND LATAM GOLD MINERS MOST EXPOSED IN H2 2026
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for July 7 identifies diesel fuel — running near $70 per barrel for bunker and inland equivalents used by mining operations — as the stealth cost driver most likely to compress margins at open-pit gold mines in H2 2026, with the analysis estimating fuel represents 15-20% of total cash costs at large-scale surface operations in Africa and Latin America. Underground mines are less exposed due to their lower diesel consumption per ounce, giving a structural cost advantage to underground-focused jurisdictions like Ontario's Red Lake camp or Quebec's Abitibi over large open-pit operations in West Africa or the Andes. The fuel-cost analysis is a useful input for comparing operating cost trajectories across the junior mining universe: companies advancing underground projects or in low-fuel-cost jurisdictions carry a meaningful but often-overlooked margin advantage relative to open-pit peers as oil prices remain elevated.

headline: TOREX GOLD Q2 2026 PRODUCTION RESULTS — MEDIA LUNA RAMP CONTINUES AS DUAL-CATALYST DAY COMBINES WITH LOS REYES PEA (TSX:TXG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Torex Gold Resources Inc.
snippet: Torex Gold Resources (TSX:TXG) released its Q2 2026 production results on July 7 — the same day as the Los Reyes PEA — making it a dual-catalyst trading session for the stock with both backward-looking operational confirmation and forward-looking economic assessment released simultaneously. Media Luna, the El Limón Deep–Media Luna underground complex in Guerrero, Mexico, has been ramping up production since achieving commercial production in 2024 and the Q2 update reflects the operating trajectory of one of Canada's newest mid-tier gold underground mines. The dual-release approach — operational results and development economics on the same day — is an unusual move that signals Torex's intent to reframe its investment case from a single-mine producer to a multi-asset growth story, with the Q2 figures providing the balance sheet context investors need to evaluate whether Los Reyes development capital is fundable from operating cash flow.
